options.rationale: Sepsis from pyelonephritis in diabetic patient. qSOFA: RR≥22 + SBP≤100 + AMS = high risk for poor outcomes. IV fluids (30mL/kg crystalloid). Empiric abx: piperacillin-tazobactam or ceftriaxone + aminoglycoside. Source control: US to rule out abscess/obstruction.
Septic (BP 85/50) with organ dysfunction = severe sepsis. Requires IV abx, IV fluids, monitoring.
Antibiotics should not be delayed in sepsis. Give abx within 1 hour of recognition.
Septic patient needs IV antibiotics for reliable bioavailability. Oral = insufficient for severe infection.

rationale: Sepsis from pyelonephritis in diabetic patient. qSOFA: RR≥22 + SBP≤100 + AMS = high risk for poor outcomes

question: A 55-year-old with crushing substernal chest pain 2h. ECG: ST elevation II, III, aVF.

options.text: PCI within 90 min (or fibrinolysis if PCI unavailable)
options.rationale: Inferior STEMI (RCA occlusion). Door-to-balloon <90 min PCI, door-to-needle <30 min. MONA: Morphine + O2 + NTG + Aspirin 324mg + ticagrelor 180mg + heparin. Check RV involvement: V4R, avoid nitrates if RV infarct.
STEMI requires REPERFUSION, not just medical management. NTG is symptomatic only.
CTA for low-intermediate probability. STEMI has diagnostic ECG → direct to PCI.

rationale: Inferior STEMI (RCA occlusion). Door-to-balloon <90 min PCI, door-to-needle <30 min

question: A 20-year-old acute severe asthma: cannot speak full sentences, RR 32, O2 sat 88%, PEFR 30%.

options.text: Continuous albuterol + ipratropium + IV methylprednisolone + consider BiPAP

Severe (cannot speak, O2 88%) requires aggressive ED management, not outpatient therapy.

question: A 65-year-old: acute severe tearing chest pain radiating to back. BP 200/110 right arm, 140/80 left. CXR: widened mediastinum.

options.text: CT angiogram chest/abdomen/pelvis + IV labetalol to reduce BP

options.text: CT head to rule out stroke

question: A 5-year-old toxic appearing with fever, petechial/purpuric rash, meningismus. BP 70/40, cap refill 4s.
